mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Federal Funds Rate signals monetary tightening, compressing discount rates on equity cash flows and reducing future growth expectations, leading to negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite a sustained rise in FEDFUNDS, or the relationship is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a t-test over the 20-day horizon).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) indicates strengthening labor markets, boosting economic growth and corporate earnings, which drives positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative despite a sustained decline in UNRATE, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a t-test over the 5-day horizon).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in GDP growth (GDPC1) reflects robust economic activity, boosting corporate profits and equity valuations, resulting in positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative despite rising GDPC1, or the relationship is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a t-test over the 60-day horizon).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate is below 2% and the unemployment rate falls below its previous month's level, the combined effect of monetary easing and improving labor markets signals strong growth, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 2% and UNRATE < previous month's UNRATE value
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative despite FEDFUNDS <2% and UNRATE falling below previous month's level, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a multivariate regression over the 5-day horizon).

mechanism_narrative: When GDP growth (GDPC1) and industrial production (INDPRO) both exceed their 3-month moving averages, the confluence of strong demand and supply signals robust economic expansion, leading to positive 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative despite both GDPC1 and INDPRO exceeding their 3-month averages, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a multivariate regression over the 60-day horizon).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in the unemployment rate below 8% during a late-cycle expansion signals labor market strength and economic momentum, driving positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns remain negative despite UNRATE falling below 8% in a late-cycle expansion, or the effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a t-test over the 5-day horizon).

mechanism_narrative: When the Federal Funds Rate exceeds 2% and demand (HOUST) rises above its 3-month average, conflicting signals of monetary tightening and robust demand create market uncertainty, resulting in negative 20-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns remain positive despite FEDFUNDS >2% and HOUST above 3-month average, or the interaction effect is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a multivariate regression over the 20-day horizon).

mechanism_narrative: During a sustained monetary tightening cycle (evidenced by rising FEDFUNDS for 3 months), elevated discount rates on future cash flows reduce equity valuations, leading to negative 60-day S&P 500 forward returns.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain positive during a sustained monetary tightening cycle (FEDFUNDS rising for 3 months), or the relationship is not statistically significant (p > 0.05 in a t-test over the 60-day horizon).
